title: Make the build bot say which build finished, and how

blocks.text: The CI server posts build news to the team channel. When a build is scheduled, its `BuildJob` hands the build agent two callbacks: one the agent calls for each progress report, and one it runs when the build is over, often many minutes later. In the old version the channel filled with lines like `practice.BuildJob$2@6d06d69c: queued`, which named no build and reported every build as still queued.

items: `completionCallback()`: posts `<job>: <status>`, with the status the build has when the callback runs.

blocks.text: `<job>` is what the job's own `toString()` returns. About two lines in total.

cases.says: each progress report posts the build's name and the percentage
the completion callback posts nothing when it is made and exactly one line when it runs
the completion line names the build job itself, not the callback object
the completion line carries the status the build has when the callback runs, not when it was made

origin.section: A Lambda Adds No Scope: `this` and Every Name Mean What They Mean Outside It

concepts: A lambda that uses a field captures this and reads the field when it runs; a field copied into a local first is frozen at that moment.
Inside a lambda, this and unqualified methods mean the enclosing instance; inside an anonymous class they mean the anonymous object.
